 13 November 2026
 CCPI 2027: India Slips to 28th Position in Global Climate Change Performance Index 
 Prelims: COP31, Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), Renewable Energy, Paris Agreement.
 Mains: GS Paper III – Environmental Conservation, Climate Change, Energy Transition and Sustainable Development.
 Keywords: CCPI 2027, COP31, Climate Action, Net Zero Emissions, Carbon Sink, Energy Security, Renewable Energy, Fossil Fuels. 
 Why in News? 
 India has slipped five positions to 28th place in the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2027, released on the sidelines of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye. Despite significant progress in renewable energy, India retained its overall ‘medium’ performance rating due to continued coal dependence and inadequate energy infrastructure. 
 About the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 
 The CCPI is an independent monitoring tool that evaluates countries' performance in combating climate change. 
 It has been published annually since 2005. 
 Published by: Germanwatch and NewClimate Institute. 
 Coverage: 64 countries and the European Union, accounting for over 90% of global greenhouse gas emissions. 
 Objective : To promote transparency, accountability and international cooperation in climate action. 
 It assesses countries' progress towards achieving the objectives of the Paris Agreement.  
 Key Findings of CCPI 2027 
 India's Ranking : India ranked 28th with a score of 60.85, declining five positions from the previous edition. 
 Global Leader : Denmark secured fourth position with 84.05 points, becoming the highest-ranked country for the sixth consecutive year. 
 Vacant Positions: The first three positions remain vacant as no country achieved an overall ‘very high’ rating. 
 G20 Performance : Ten G20 countries received ‘very low’ ratings, while the United Kingdom was the only G20 country with a ‘high’ rating. 
 European Union: The EU secured 19th position with a ‘medium’ rating. 
 Lowest-Ranked G20 Countrie s: Saudi Arabia (65th), Russia (66th) and the United States (67th).

 India's Achievements in Climate Action 
 Renewable Energy Expansion: India received a ‘high’ rating for its renewable energy trend, particularly solar and wind energy development. 
 Non-Fossil Fuel Capacity: India achieved 50% of its installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources in June 2025, five years ahead of its original target. 
 Rooftop Solar: Government initiatives have encouraged decentralised solar electricity generation. 
 Electric Mobility: Growing adoption of electric vehicles is supporting the transition towards cleaner transportation. 
 Domestic Manufacturing: Production incentives are strengthening domestic solar equipment manufacturing. 
 India's Climate Commitments 
 Under its updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), India aims to achieve the following targets: 
 Climate Target 
 Commitment 
 Emissions intensity 
 47% reduction from 2005 levels by 2035 
 Non-fossil electricity capacity 
 Approximately 60% by 2035 
 Additional carbon sink 
 3.5–4 billion tonnes of CO ₂ equivalent through forest and tree cover 
 Net Zero Emissions 
 By 2070 
 Note: Non-fossil electricity capacity includes renewable energy and nuclear power. Installed capacity does not necessarily represent actual electricity generation. 
 Challenges Highlighted by the Report 
 Dependence on Coal: Coal continues to play a major role in India's electricity generation, increasing greenhouse gas emissions. 
 Inadequate Grid Infrastructure : Electricity transmission and storage infrastructure are struggling to accommodate the rapid expansion of renewable energy. 
 Renewable Energy Curtailment : India curtailed around 2.3 TWh of solar electricity between late May and December 2025 to maintain grid stability. 
 Fossil Fuel Imports : Dependence on imported crude oil, natural gas and coal creates economic and energy security challenges. 
 Rising Energy Demand : I ndustrialisation, urbanisation and economic development are increasing energy consumption and per-capita emissions. 
 India's Response to the Report 
 The Union Environment Ministry questioned the assessment, highlighting India's rapid progress in clean energy development. 
 India emphasised its early achievement of the 2030 non-fossil electricity capacity target. 
 The government maintained that coal remains essential for meeting India's growing energy and developmental requirements. 
 India's position reflects the need to balance climate mitigation with energy security, economic growth and developmental priorities.

 Significance of CCPI for India 
 Policy Evaluation: Helps assess the effectiveness of India's climate policies. 
 International Accountability : Encourages countries to fulfil their climate commitments. 
 Energy Transition : Highlights infrastructure gaps in clean energy adoption. 
 Climate Investmen t: Can guide investment towards low-carbon technologies. 
 Sustainable Developmen t: Encourages a balance between economic growth and environmental protection. 
 Way Forward 
 Accelerate the development of battery storage and modern electricity grids. 
 Prepare a comprehensive roadmap for reducing fossil fuel dependence. 
 Promote energy efficiency and cleaner industrial technologies. 
 Strengthen investment in green hydrogen and renewable energy. 
 Ensure a just energy transition for coal-dependent communities. 
 Enhance international cooperation on climate finance and technology transfer. 
 Conclusion 
 India's declining CCPI ranking highlights the gap between renewable energy expansion and actual decarbonisation. Achieving long-term climate objectives requires modern energy infrastructure, reduced fossil fuel dependence and a balanced approach towards sustainable development and energy security. 
 Prelims Practice Questions 
 Q. With reference to the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), consider the following statements: 
 It is published by Germanwatch and NewClimate Institute. 
 Greenhouse gas emissions receive the highest weightage in the index. 
 Denmark secured first position in CCPI 2027. 
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct? 
 (a) 1 and 2 only 
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3 
 Mains Practice Question 
 Q. Despite significant progress in renewable energy expansion, India's performance in the Climate Change Performance Index has declined. Discuss the major challenges in India's energy transition and suggest measures to achieve its long-term climate commitments. 
 FAQs 
 Q1. What is India's rank in CCPI 2027? 
 India secured 28th position with 60.85 points. 
 Q2. Who publishes the Climate Change Performance Index? 
 Germanwatch and NewClimate Institute jointly publish this index. 
 Q3. Which country topped the CCPI 2027 rankings? 
 Denmark emerged as the highest-ranked country, securing fourth position. 
 Q4. Why are the first three CCPI positions vacant? 
 No country achieved the required overall performance standards. 
 Q5. What is India's net-zero emissions target year? 
 India aims to achieve net-zero emissions by 2070. 
 Children's Day 2026 (Bal Diwas): History, Significance and Child Rights in India 
 Why in news? 
 Children's Day 2026 will be celebrated across India on 14 November 2026 (Saturday) . The day is popularly known as Bal Diwas . 
 History of Children's Day in India 
 14 November 1889: Jawaharlal Nehru was born in Allahabad (present-day Prayagraj), Uttar Pradesh. 
 He became independent India's first Prime Minister in 1947. 
 Nehru was popularly known as Chacha Nehru because of his affection for children. 
 Children's Day was associated with 14 November during Nehru's lifetime. His 1957 speech explicitly referred to the occasion as Children's Day. 
 After his death on 27 May 1964 , 14 November continued to be commemorated as Children's Day in his memory. 
 Why is Children's Day Celebrated? 
 Promoting Education: Ensuring access to quality education for every child. 
 Child Protection: Preventing child labour, child trafficking, abuse and exploitation. 
 Health and Nutrition: Improving children's healthcare, nutrition and overall well-being. 
 Equal Opportunities: Ensuring that every child gets equal opportunities irrespective of gender, caste, economic background or disability. 
 Awareness of Child Rights : Educating society about the rights and dignity of children.

 National Policy for Children, 2013 
 The Government of India adopted the National Policy for Children on 26 April 2013 . 
 It recognises every person below 18 years of age as a child. 
 The policy identifies four major priority areas: 
 Survival : Right to life and survival. 
 Health and Nutrition : Access to healthcare and adequate nutrition. 
 Education and Development: Opportunities for education and overall development. 
 Protection and Participation: Protection against exploitation and the right to participate in decisions affecting children.

 Major Challenges Related to Child Welfare in India 
 Child Labour: Children continue to face economic exploitation and loss of educational opportunities. 
 Child Marriage: Early marriage affects education, health and personal development, particularly among girls. 
 Child Abus e: Physical, emotional and sexual abuse threaten children's safety. 
 Gender Discrimination: Unequal opportunities affect girls' education, nutrition and development. 
 School Dropouts : Poverty, lack of infrastructure and social barriers affect educational continuity. 
 Prelims MCQs 
 Q. Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years? 
 A. Article 19 
 B. Article 21 
 C. Article 21A 
 D. Article 45 
 Mains Practice Question 
 Q. Examine the constitutional and legislative framework for the protection of child rights in India.  
 FAQs 
 When is Children's Day celebrated in India? 
 14 November 
 Who adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child? 
 The United Nations General Assembly in 1989. 
 What is the legal definition of a child under the National Policy for Children, 2013? 
 Every person below 18 years of age. 
 Which constitutional amendment introduced Article 21A? 
 The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. 
 Which organisation is responsible for monitoring child rights protection laws in India? 
 The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR).
